label: L13 · Spirochetes & Syphilis
rows: Gram-negative spirals; ENDOFLAGELLA inside the cell; Treponema, Leptospira, Borrelia; may have LINEAR deoxyribonucleic acid and plasmids (Borrelia).
Humans the only natural host; extremely fastidious; dies outside the host; needs LIVE CELLS to culture. Sexual + transplacental.
Binds mucous membrane or abraded skin → penetrates capillaries → circulation. Communicable in PRIMARY and SECONDARY.
Primary: HARD chancre, heals · secondary: fever, sore throat, rash on PALMS and SOLES · tertiary: GUMMAS, neuro, cardiovascular, Argyll Robertson pupil.
Transplacental: SNUFFLES, skin eruptions, bone deformation (HUTCHINSON'S TEETH), nervous system.

Dark-field · rapid plasma reagin (antibodies) · VDRL (Venereal Disease Research Laboratory; the older version) · FTA-ABS (fluorescent treponemal antibody-absorption). Penicillin G or doxycycline. False-positive reagin: human immunodeficiency virus, Lyme, malaria, lupus.
Rarely sexual/congenital. BEJEL (endemicum, childhood mouth) · YAWS (pertenue, skin cut → second crop) · PINTA (carateum, depigments).

label: L13 · Leptospira & Borrelia
rows: HOOKED ends. L. interrogans: zoonosis via mammal URINE; moisture. Surfers, vets, farmers, slaughterhouse. Fever, CONJUNCTIVITIS; kidneys and liver.
B. hermsii; squirrels, chipmunks, rodents; antigen CHANGES → febrile/afebrile cycles. Tetracycline.
B. burgdorferi; WHITE-FOOTED MOUSE + IXODES ticks; 2-year cycle with deer; humans accidental hosts.
ERYTHEMA MIGRANS (bull's-eye); flu-like; untreated → cardiac, neurological, polyarthritis. Tetracycline or amoxicillin.
DEET (diethyltoluamide) repellent + tick checks. Dog vaccine yes; human vaccine WITHDRAWN.

label: L13 · Vibrio, Campylobacter & Helicobacter
rows: Vibrio: COMMA, single polar flagellum · Campylobacter: curved/S, one flagellum · Helicobacter: tight spirals, SEVERAL polar flagella.
Contaminated WATER; large dose (must pass the stomach); small intestine, NONINVASIVE; toxin → secretory 'RICE WATER' stool. Oral rehydration + tetracycline; vaccine. El Tor survives longer.
V. parahaemolyticus: RAW SEAFOOD, cholera-like. V. vulnificus: RAW OYSTERS; severe in DIABETES or LIVER disease; 'flesh-eating'. Fluids first.
GULL-WINGED; water, milk, meat, CHICKEN; end of small intestine; heat-labile enterotoxin; bloody or watery diarrhea; rehydration.
Opportunist: DEBILITATED or LATE PREGNANCY; newborn meningitis, septicemia; sexually transmitted in cattle, sheep, goats.
Warren and Marshall (Nobel); stomach and duodenal ULCERS; gastric cancer cofactor; UREASE → raises local pH. Biopsy urease gel: positive at pH 6.5+.

label: L13 · Rickettsias, Coxiella, Bartonella
rows: SMALLEST bacteria; obligate INTRACELLULAR; Gram-negative; nonmotile coccobacilli; ticks, fleas, lice; ENDOTHELIAL cells → vasculitis, leakage, thrombosis.
EPIDEMIC: R. prowazekii, LICE (recurrent form Brill-Zinsser) · ENDEMIC (murine): R. typhi, FLEAS of mice and rats, milder.
R. rickettsii; DOG and WOOD ticks; Southeast + eastern seaboard; spotted rash (mistaken for MEASLES); heart, central nervous system.
Cross-reaction between PROTEUS and R. prowazekii.
Tick-borne rickettsias; E. chaffeensis = human MONOCYTIC ehrlichiosis.
Q FEVER ('query'); resistant endospore; INHALED (urine, feces, milk, air) → pneumonitis, liver inflammation. Tetracycline; vaccine for veterinarians, farmers, laboratory technicians.
Fastidious, blood agar. TRENCH FEVER (lice) · CAT-SCRATCH disease · bacillary angiomatosis in acquired immunodeficiency syndrome. Tetracycline, erythromycin, rifampin.
The recurring drug: broad spectrum, prokaryotic 30S ribosome.

label: L13 · Chlamydias, Mycoplasmas & Teeth
rows: ELEMENTARY: small, inactive, extracellular, INFECTIOUS · RETICULATE: dividing, noninfectious, in vacuoles, cannot make its own adenosine triphosphate.
Human reservoir. Ocular TRACHOMA → blindness · inclusion conjunctivitis (BIRTH CANAL) · top sexually transmitted infection (pelvic inflammatory disease, infertility) · lymphogranuloma venereum.
C. pneumoniae: atypical pneumonia, serious in ASTHMA · C. psittaci: ORNITHOSIS from BIRDS.

NO cell wall (no peptidoglycan → not penicillin; tetracycline or erythromycin); pleomorphic; needs host lipids. M. pneumoniae: primary ATYPICAL pneumonia. M. genitalium, Ureaplasma: weak sexually transmitted pathogens.
Most commonly diagnosed disease. Slime-forming Streptococcus (S. MUTANS) + Actinomyces → PLAQUE → ACID dissolves enamel; secondary Lactobacillus, Bacteroides, Fusobacterium.
Calcified plaque = CALCULUS → GINGIVITIS → pockets of spirochetes + Gram-negative bacilli → PERIODONTITIS → tooth loss.
